content.value_statement: Academic reviews can be inconsistent and difficult to compare across drafts. This skill applies structured ScholarEval criteria to produce clear scores, evidence-based feedback, and revision priorities.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates research papers, proposals, theses, literature reviews, and conference abstracts.
Assesses problem formulation, literature review, methodology, data, analysis, results, writing, and citations.
Provides dimension-level strengths, weaknesses, and optional 1 to 5 scores.
Synthesizes overall quality, publication readiness, and priority recommendations.
Uses a local Python helper to calculate weighted aggregate scores from dimension ratings.
limitations: Does not replace expert peer review or discipline-specific judgment.
Requires the user to provide the scholarly work or sufficient excerpts for evaluation.
Score quality depends on accurate dimension ratings and appropriate context settings.
Some rubric dimensions may not apply to theoretical or early-stage work.

use_cases.title: Review a journal manuscript draft
use_cases.description: Assess quality across research dimensions and identify revisions needed before submission.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a thesis chapter
use_cases.description: Provide structured feedback on clarity, methodology, evidence, and citation quality.

use_cases.title: Compare research proposals
use_cases.description: Apply the same rubric to several proposals and summarize relative strengths and risks.

prompt_templates.title: Basic manuscript evaluation
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you want a clear review of one paper draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this research paper using ScholarEval. Focus on strengths, weaknesses, and the top three revisions needed before submission.

prompt_templates.title: Dimension-specific review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when one part of the work needs deeper feedback.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ScholarEval to evaluate only the methodology, analysis, and results sections. Provide evidence from the text and rate each dimension from 1 to 5.

prompt_templates.title: Publication readiness assessment
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before submitting to a journal or conference.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether this manuscript is ready for submission to the target venue. Use ScholarEval criteria and separate blocking issues from optional improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Comparative proposal review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when ranking or triaging multiple research proposals.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these research proposals with the same ScholarEval rubric. Compare problem significance, feasibility, methodology, and expected contribution, then recommend a priority order.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a machine learning paper for publication readiness.
output: Overall assessment with publication readiness level
Dimension scores for methodology, analysis, results, writing, and citations
Prioritized revision list with evidence from the draft

output_examples.input: Review a literature review chapter for a thesis.
output: Specific recommendations to improve structure and gap identification

output_examples.input: Compare three research proposals for a funding program.

best_practices: Provide the full paper or clearly labeled sections so evidence can be cited precisely.
State the work stage, discipline, and target venue before requesting scores.
Use the same rubric settings when comparing drafts or multiple submissions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat numeric scores as a substitute for expert domain review.
Do not request a final publication decision without providing the target venue context.
Do not evaluate only the abstract when asking for methodology or analysis feedback.

faq.question: What types of scholarly work can this skill evaluate?
faq.answer: It can evaluate research papers, proposals, literature reviews, thesis chapters, conference abstracts, and similar academic drafts.

faq.question: Does it provide numeric scores?
faq.answer: Yes. It can provide optional 1 to 5 scores for each applicable ScholarEval dimension and summarize the overall score.

faq.question: Can it replace peer review?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured feedback, but expert reviewers should make final academic and publication decisions.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the draft, its purpose, the discipline, the work stage, and any target venue or evaluation criteria.

faq.question: Can it compare multiple submissions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can apply the same rubric to multiple works and summarize comparative strengths, weaknesses, and priorities.

faq.question: Does it run external services automatically?
faq.answer: No. The core evaluation uses local rubric guidance. Any optional diagram generation described in the skill requires separate user action.
